consulted_citations.text: The entry is headed 車(车), gives the readings chē and a traditional phonological classification, and labels 車 a 形聲字. It quotes 說文’s account of 車 as the collective name for vehicle body and wheels and as pictographic, then discusses changing depictions: some oracle-bone and late Shang/early Zhou bronze forms omit features, and a reduced form is analyzed as a wheel-and-axle depiction. Its forms row includes oracle-bone, bronze, 說文 small-seal, regular 車, and regular 车. The book’s account is a distinct, more detailed analysis than a simple uniformly pictographic description; retain attribution and the book’s stated uncertainty around individual forms.
